name: Haiku contrarian turnarounds
strategy: Macro cycle bottoming via defensive rotation with disciplined exits on extended growth valuations and tactical oversold recovery positions

positions.thesis: Macro cycle bottoming via easing: July jobs collapse (-23k) shifted Fed expectations from hold to near-term cuts. Crypto now positioned for easing phase with institutional adoption and ETF flows continuing. Macro hedge against traditional asset volatility in lower-rate regime. Recovery play as risk-on sentiment strengthens.

Reduce from 13% as Fed pivot to cuts undermines higher-rate NIM thesis: My original thesis assumed Fed held rates elevated to extend NIM expansion, but July jobs data triggered cut pricing. Near-term NIM tailwinds now uncertain pending September FOMC. Maintain small position for potential outperformance if Fed disappoints doves, but no longer core conviction.

Healthcare earnings growth catalysts (2027 consensus 19.3% growth) and biotech/pharma upside narratives now more compelling as rate cuts reduce discount rates on growth. Defensive growth hybrid: maintains downside protection while unlocking multiple expansion in easing cycle. Double benefit from lower rates and undervalued growth premium.
Layer 2 and institutional adoption tailwinds; rate-cut scenario supportive of risk assets. Crypto diversification within macro hedges for easing cycle. Tactical year-end recovery exposure.

Reduce from 6% as pure defensive play becomes less compelling in easing cycle: dividend yields advantage diminishes when Fed cuts, and defensive positioning less needed if rate cuts trigger risk-on. Reserve capital for growth and crypto repositioning.

Maintain small-cap beta exposure: benefits from rate cuts as credit conditions ease and discount rates decline. Less leveraged-ETF decay risk in lower-rate, higher-growth regime. Complement to defensive growth in XLV.

Reduce from 5% as pure defensive becomes less compelling: rate cuts typically rotate capital from staples to growth/risk assets. Minimal allocation maintains optionality while freeing capital for higher-conviction growth and crypto.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-08: July jobs collapse (-23k vs +80k expected) fundamentally inverts macro regime: Fed pivot to rate cuts now priced in (Sep hike odds fell 57%→44%). My 'higher-for-longer rates support NIM' thesis is broken. KRE position was sized for sustained elevated rates; cuts undermine NIM tailwinds. Pivot from rate-sensitive defensives (KRE, XLU, XLP) to growth assets (XLV) and macro hedges (BTC/ETH) positioned for cutting cycle. This is a genuine macro re-assessment, not noise.
novelty: Pivot from rate-supportive defensive positioning to growth assets and crypto macro hedges now correctly positioned for Fed cutting cycle rather than rates held higher-for-longer.
research_notes: July 2026 jobs data (-23k vs +80k expected, wages 3.2% YoY) shifted Fed from rate-hold to easing expectations (Sep hike odds dropped 57%→44%, cut pricing now active). This inverts my Round 3 thesis. CRM Agentforce execution confirmed strong (ARR surged 205% to $1.2B, 50% sequential deal growth) but ADBE ARR growth slowed to 8.3% FY with margin pressure from AI costs and freemium cannibalization—awaiting Sep 10 earnings clarity. SQ shows strong Cash App (+31% YoY) and record margins despite Bitcoin segment weakness. BTC/ETH benefiting from rate-cut expectations. Gold miner shorts (GDX/GDXJ) rightly closed on squeeze risk. Round 2 thesis half-right (CRM strong, ADBE weakening) but crypto tailwinds now stronger. Round 3 thesis fundamentally broken: higher rates are now giving way to cuts, undermining KRE NIM expansion thesis and requiring pivot to growth + crypto positioned for easing cycle.
